# Part IX: Infrastructure, Compute, and Frontiers {#part-infrastructure .unnumbered}

> "The free lunch is over."
>
> Herb Sutter, ["Welcome to the Jungle"](https://herbsutter.com/welcome-to-the-jungle/)

The stack can be drawn as software, but its lower layers are stubbornly physical.
Chips have memory pins. Clusters have network tiers. Checkpoints cross storage
systems. Power arrives on a schedule measured in years. Failure appears not as an
exceptional event but as a statistical certainty. This part goes beneath the
model and asks what the machine makes possible before the math begins.

@sec-accelerators-networking starts with bandwidth, the hidden shape behind many
training and serving decisions. @sec-orchestration-data-infra shows how long runs
survive failure, keep accelerators fed, and remain observable. @sec-compute-frontier
and @sec-making-silicon move from racks to packages, HBM, supply chains, and the
geography of compute. @sec-powering-ai adds the constraint that often arrives
last in conversation and first in deployment: power. @sec-machine-breaks follows
the failures that become inevitable at scale. @sec-learning-limits asks what
happens when data, feedback, and learnable signal run thin. @sec-capability-horizon
then returns to measurement, where the frontier is less a single score than a
horizon whose instruments keep saturating.

Read this part as a reminder that intelligence runs on infrastructure. Every
elegant modeling decision eventually becomes traffic, heat, memory pressure, a
supply chain, or an operating procedure. The frontier is not only where
capability grows. It is where constraints become visible.
